issues.description: Deprecation message duplicates info already in the docstring directive
issues.detail: The deprecation warning string and the .. deprecated:: 4.3 docstring directive say the same thing twice. Small thing, but the data (the deprecation notice) lives in two places now and will drift. Keeping the canonical text in one spot and referencing it would be cleaner.

The deprecation directive in the docstring reads 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`...'. Minor, but it's the user-facing breadcrumb pointing them to the replacement. Worth fixing while you're touching the file.

issues.description: Test does not assert the deprecation actually fires for stderr path
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected only exercises the stdout branch. The function takes both stdout and stderr; if you're paying the cost of a test, cover both inputs so the data the function transforms is fully represented. Small addition, obvious payoff.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE. This PR is exactly the kind of cleanup the Unix tradition rewards: a custom helper is being retired in favor of the stdlib filter that already does the same job, and callers are migrated one-for-one to contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr. The data shape (a TextIO sink swapped in around a block) is unchanged; the algorithm becomes self-evident once you stop wrapping it. Two small nits and one typo ('stlib') are worth fixing on the way through, plus rounding out the test to cover the stderr branch. Nothing blocks merge.
